solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Watch present and past entertainment for children

parts.note: to watch is to see, in the present tense
the past tense of see, the verb just given, is saw

explanation.surface: Watching a show now and in the past counts as fun for the kids.
explanation.walkthrough: The tenses belong to one verb: 'see' now, 'saw' before.
explanation.definitionFit: A playground plank that tips up and down is a classic children's amusement.

clue.text: Like Kate Moss, ultimately having desire to take her out?

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of the word Moss
out signals that the word her is rearranged

parts.note: a desire is a wish

explanation.surface: A tabloid quip about a model and someone eager to date her.
explanation.walkthrough: Kate is not the model but the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew; 'out' scrambles HER to HRE.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Kate is the shrew to be tamed, so she is sharp-tongued and bad-tempered.

clue.text: To root out dodgy extremists in Tunisia I exert power

indicators.note: dodgy means unreliable or crooked, so the letters are rearranged
the extremists of the word Tunisia are its outer letters

explanation.surface: Someone vows to stamp out shady radicals in Tunisia by force.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dodgy' rearranges TA (the outer letters of Tunisia) plus I, EXERT and P.
explanation.definitionFit: To pull up something by the roots is to destroy it completely, which is the sense of uproot.

clue.text: A cordon cleared out last of trouble spots

indicators.note: a word cleared out has its inside emptied, leaving only the first and last letters of cordon
last of points to the final letter of the word trouble

explanation.surface: Police tape is removed after the last disturbance at some trouble spots.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trouble spots' reads as one phrase, but 'spots' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Spots and pimples on the skin are the familiar teenage complaint.

clue.text: Management is very relaxed about bribes, on reflection?

indicators.note: on reflection means the whole construction is mirrored, read from the end
about means surrounding, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: very relaxed is laid-back, read here as the word laid
sops are small payments or concessions given to placate someone

explanation.surface: A complaint that the bosses are too easy-going about taking backhanders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Very relaxed' is laid-back, and 'on reflection' turns the whole thing round, so the 'back' of laid-back is doubly apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Disposal in the sense of control or arrangement, as in 'at your disposal', means management of something.

clue.text: Admission by married person caused damage

parts.note: an admission by a person is 'I'm', as in owning up to something
a married couple is paired

explanation.surface: A married person's confession did harm.
explanation.walkthrough: The admission a married person might make is 'I'm paired'.
explanation.definitionFit: To impair is to weaken or harm, so having impaired something means having done damage to it.

clue.text: Fellow avoids boring, long speech

indicators.note: avoids means the letter for fellow is left out of the word for boring

parts.note: boring a hole makes a perforation

explanation.surface: A man skips a dull, rambling lecture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boring' reads as dull, but it means drilling holes.
explanation.definitionFit: A peroration is the closing part of an oration, or loosely any long-winded address.

clue.text: Blade Runner to a large extent's a retro film

indicators.note: to a large extent means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: a ski is a runner on snow

indicators.note: retro means going backwards, so the film title is reversed

parts.note: ET is the Spielberg film about an extraterrestrial

explanation.surface: A claim that the sci-fi classic Blade Runner is mostly a nostalgic movie.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'Blade Runner' as the film title, but 'Blade' is the definition and 'Runner' a ski.
explanation.definitionFit: An ice skate is the steel blade fixed beneath a boot.

clue.text: Soldier needs a way out of northern city

indicators.note: out of means these letters are removed from the city's name

parts.note: Lancaster is a city in the north of England
ST is short for street, a way

explanation.surface: A soldier must find a route out of a city in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: LANCASTER is a city in north-west England; remove A and ST.
explanation.definitionFit: A lancer is a cavalryman armed with a lance.

clue.text: Trip is all but cheerful

indicators.note: all but means everything except the final letter

parts.note: jaunty means lively and cheerful

explanation.surface: An outing is described as nearly delightful.
explanation.definitionFit: A jaunt is a short pleasure excursion.

clue.text: Break out and run round building

parts.note: R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: break means smash up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An instruction to escape and race around a building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Break out' reads as escape, but 'Break' alone scrambles OUT and AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotunda is a circular building, often domed.

clue.text: Apply pressure and confident opener's dismissed

parts.note: P is the physics abbreviation for pressure

indicators.note: the opener is the first letter, and dismissed means it is removed

parts.note: being certain is being confident

explanation.surface: A cricket captain is told to press on now the cocky opening batsman is out.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opener is the first batsman; here it is the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To pertain is to apply or be relevant, as rules pertain to a case.

clue.text: Custody of daughter obtained after fighting

indicators.note: obtained after places the daughter's letter behind the word for fighting

parts.note: fighting between nations is war

explanation.surface: A parent wins custody of their daughter after a long legal battle.
explanation.definitionFit: Ward means guardianship or protective custody, as in keeping someone in ward.

clue.text: Soldier, perhaps, one with decoration, said to offer protection in the cooler

parts.note: a soldier is one caste of ant, so the 'perhaps' marks an example
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: said means spoken aloud, so the word for decoration is entered as what it sounds like

parts.note: a frieze is a decorative band along a wall

explanation.surface: A decorated soldier speaks up for a prisoner in jail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' sounds like prison slang, but it is a car's cooling system.
explanation.definitionFit: A coolant additive stops a car radiator's water from icing up in winter.

clue.text: Polite way to cough? That's out of date

definitions.meaning: politely one coughs behind one's hand
late, behind schedule or in arrears

explanation.definitionFit: Behindhand means late or in arrears; read as two words it is where the polite cougher's hand goes.

clue.text: Tartar's beginning to drink like a fish?

parts.note: tartar is the hard deposit on teeth, also called scale

indicators.note: beginning to points to the first letter of the word drink

explanation.surface: A man with stained teeth starts to drink heavily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drink like a fish' is the idiom, but 'like a fish?' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish are covered in scales, so a scaly creature is fish-like.

clue.text: Tourist outside left in distress becomes annoyed

indicators.note: in places the letters inside the word for distress

parts.note: need means hardship or distress

indicators.note: outside points to the outer letters of the word Tourist

explanation.surface: A tourist left stranded in trouble gets irritated.
explanation.definitionFit: To be nettled is to be irritated, as if stung by a nettle.

clue.text: English criminal tried at last in Bordeaux? Hand him over.

indicators.note: last in points to the final letter of the word Bordeaux
criminal means crooked, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An English criminal tried in a French city should be sent home.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Criminal' looks like a noun but scrambles TRIED AT; 'at last' is a false phrase, the 'last' going with 'in Bordeaux'.
explanation.definitionFit: To extradite is to surrender an accused person to another country's authorities.

clue.text: Jana pole dancing is something really hot

indicators.note: dancing means moving about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pole dancer called Jana is very sexy.
explanation.definitionFit: The jalapeno is a fiery Mexican chilli pepper.

clue.text: Jack's dressed in extremely fancy but tawdry finery

indicators.note: dressed in means placed inside the outer letters
extremely points to the outer letters of the word fancy

parts.note: Jack the Ripper, the Victorian murderer, gives the Ripper

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack wears gaudy, cheap clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Frippery is showy, trivial ornament or cheap finery.

clue.text: Influential and revolutionary style of animation penned by Lowry?

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the whole is read backwards
penned by means enclosed within the painter's initials

parts.note: L.S. Lowry, the English painter, gives his initials
anime is the Japanese style of animation

explanation.surface: A painter's groundbreaking cartoon work proves influential.
explanation.walkthrough: L.S. Lowry painted northern English industrial scenes; 'revolutionary' turns the whole construction round, not just the animation style.
explanation.definitionFit: A seminal work strongly shapes later developments.

clue.text: Hat, one going in the junk?

definitions.meaning: a stiff straw hat with a flat crown
a junk is a Chinese sailing vessel, so someone travelling in it goes by boat

explanation.definitionFit: A boater is a straw hat and, punningly, anyone who boats.

clue.text: Talk at length? Absolutely right!

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means drone on, and the adjective means precisely accurate.

clue.text: Mark gives up Latin as a bad job

indicators.note: gives up means the letter is dropped

parts.note: a blotch is a mark or stain

explanation.surface: A man named Mark abandons his Latin studies as hopeless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' reads as a man's name, but it is a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: A botch is a clumsy, spoiled piece of work.

clue.text: Church dignitary maintaining firm support at first for another

indicators.note: at first puts the support at the front of the construction

parts.note: an arch is a supporting structure

indicators.note: maintaining means holding, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a dean is a senior cleric
CO is the standard abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A church official is backed by a business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Church dignitary' looks like the definition but is DEAN; 'another' is the definition, another such dignitary.
explanation.definitionFit: An archdeacon is a senior Anglican cleric ranking below a bishop, so another dignitary.

clue.text: After century, a branch of the fighting forces retains old cannon

indicators.note: After places the rest behind the century's letter

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

indicators.note: retains means holds inside

parts.words: a branch of the fighting forces
parts.note: an arm is a branch of the military, as the air arm

explanation.surface: A military unit keeps an antique artillery piece after a hundred years.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cannon' is not artillery but a billiards shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In billiards a carom, also called a cannon, is a shot striking two balls in turn.

clue.text: It is used to grate fruit

explanation.definitionFit: A rasp is a coarse file, and also an informal name for a raspberry.

clue.text: For example Sutherland (Donald) is versatile actor, taking leading parts

indicators.note: the leading parts of words are their first letters

explanation.surface: The actor Donald Sutherland is praised for his range in starring roles.
explanation.walkthrough: Not Donald Sutherland but Joan Sutherland, the Australian soprano.
explanation.definitionFit: Joan Sutherland was a celebrated operatic soprano, a prima donna.

clue.text: Two Europeans may be closely related

parts.note: a German is one European
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Two people from Europe may be kin.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant or pertinent, closely connected to the matter.

clue.text: Scouser regularly eats one's home cooking

indicators.note: a Scouser who eats a meal takes it inside, so these letters swallow the other pieces
regularly picks every other letter of the word Scouser

parts.note: one's is read as I's, the numeral I plus S
at home is in

explanation.surface: A Liverpudlian often has a meal at home.
explanation.walkthrough: A Scouser is someone from Liverpool. 'Home cooking' reads as one phrase, but 'home' is IN.
explanation.definitionFit: Cuisine is a style of cooking.

clue.text: Pardon me being disposed to show off

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A request for pardon from someone inclined to boast.
explanation.definitionFit: To name-drop is to mention famous acquaintances to impress others.

clue.text: Yankee's after cent off angel cake bought here?

indicators.note: after places the Yankee's letter at the end
off means the letter for cent is removed

parts.note: an angel is a financial backer of a show
Y is Yankee in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An American buys angel cake at a discount.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Angel cake' is a false phrase: angel is a theatrical BACKER.
explanation.definitionFit: A bakery is a shop selling bread and cakes.
